extracted.intended_audience: researchers and nominators preparing submissions for the Dreyfus Prize in the Chemical Sciences
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting a nomination for the Dreyfus Prize in the Chemical Sciences, including eligibility, topic scope, required documents, page/word limits, and letter-of-support procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / selection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dreyfus Prize in the Chemical Sciences is awarded to an individual in a selected area of chemistry to recognize exceptional and original research that has advanced the field in a major way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations should document exceptional, original research with major impact on the field. The award is for a single individual's cited advance; materials should emphasize the originality and significance of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2027 topic: Chemical Probes of Biological Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: 2027 Topic — Chemical Probes of Biological Systems: The development of probes to understand biological function, particularly in the context of cells or organisms, is an important discipline in the chemical sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations for 2027 should relate to development of probes (distinct from imaging technologies) that reveal functions of biological molecules (proteins, glycans, nucleic acids), regulation of pathways, and understanding of disease mechanisms. Ensure the nomination clearly links the nominee's work to this topic scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection: awarded to an individual; interdisciplinary clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Prize is awarded to an individual. If the cited advance is substantially interdisciplinary, those aspects that represent original chemistry should be clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not nominate teams; ensure the nomination isolates and explains the nominee's individual contribution. For interdisciplinary work, explicitly identify and describe the 'original chemistry' components that justify the chemistry prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: who may / may not be nominated
rubrics_metrics.description: The Prize is open to international nominations. Present Dreyfus Foundation Directors, Advisors, and consultants, as well as previous Dreyfus Prize winners, and Nobel Laureates are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no restriction on nominees' country of residence or institutional affiliation. Verify the nominee is not a current Foundation Director/Advisor/consultant, a past Dreyfus Prize winner, or a Nobel Laureate before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional limits / approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no restriction on the number of nominees from a given institution, nor is institutional approval required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators do not need to obtain institutional sign-off and institutions may submit multiple nominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may nominate / self-nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may nominate a candidate for the Dreyfus Prize. Self-nominations are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations must be submitted by someone other than the nominee. Ensure the nominator is willing to request letters of support as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required: online nomination form
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the Foundation's online form as part of the nomination package in addition to the other required documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required: nomination letter (three-page limit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The nomination letter should summarize the nominee's qualifying achievements and fit to the prize topic and must not exceed three pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required: CV (five-page limit; include degree and advisor)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CV that includes highest degree and advisor (five-page limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the CV to five pages and explicitly list the nominee's highest degree and advisor. Focus the CV on information relevant to assessing the cited advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required: list of up to ten papers and/or patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of up to ten total papers and/or patents relating to the nomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a curated list (maximum 10) of publications and patents that most directly support the nomination; do not exceed ten items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required: provisional citation (30-word limit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a concise 30-word or shorter citation summarizing the reason for the award (used for announcement/medal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format and address
rubrics_metrics.description: Send all the above materials by the deadline as a single PDF to: [email protected].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble the nomination form output and required documents into one single PDF and submit to the specified Foundation email by the deadline. Follow naming/ordering conventions if any are provided elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support: number, format, length, and submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to three letters of support are accepted for each nomination. Letters should be PDFs and no more than three pages. Letters are to be requested by the nominator and sent directly to the Foundation at [email protected]. Letters of support should not be received with the nomination package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators must request letters (max 3) from recommenders; recommenders should send each letter as a PDF (≤3 pages) directly to the Foundation email rather than bundling them into the nominee's single-PDF package. Ensure recommenders submit by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important dates / deadline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All nomination materials and supporting letters must be submitted by the stated deadline; plan ahead to allow recommenders time to send letters directly to the Foundation.
